21: const animationNameRE = /^(-\w+-)?animation-name$/
22: const animationRE = /^(-\w+-)?animation$/
23: 
24: const scopedPlugin: PluginCreator<string> = (id = '') => {
25:   const keyframes = Object.create(null)
26:   const shortId = id.replace(/^data-v-/, '')
27:   const rewriter = new ScopedSelectorRewriter(id)
28:   const units = createSelectorRewriteUnits()
29: 
30:   return {
31:     postcssPlugin: 'vue-sfc-scoped',
32:     Rule(rule) {
33:       processRule(rule, rewriter, units)
34:     },
35:     AtRule(node) {
36:       if (
37:         /-?keyframes$/.test(node.name) &&
38:         !node.params.endsWith(`-${shortId}`)
39:       ) {
40:         // register keyframes
41:         keyframes[node.params] = node.params = node.params + '-' + shortId
42:       }
43:     },
44:     OnceExit(root) {
45:       if (Object.keys(keyframes).length) {
46:         // If keyframes are found in this <style>, find and rewrite animation names
47:         // in declarations.
48:         // Caveat: this only works for keyframes and animation rules in the same
49:         // <style> element.
50:         // individual animation-name declaration
51:         root.walkDecls(decl => {
52:           if (animationNameRE.test(decl.prop)) {
53:             decl.value = decl.value
54:               .split(',')
55:               .map(v => keyframes[v.trim()] || v.trim())
56:               .join(',')
57:           }
58:           // shorthand
59:           if (animationRE.test(decl.prop)) {
60:             decl.value = decl.value
61:               .split(',')
62:               .map(v => {
63:                 const vals = v.trim().split(/\s+/)
64:                 const i = vals.findIndex(val => keyframes[val])
65:                 if (i !== -1) {
66:                   vals.splice(i, 1, keyframes[vals[i]])
67:                   return vals.join(' ')
68:                 } else {
69:                   return v
70:                 }
71:               })
72:               .join(',')
73:           }
74:         })
75:       }
76:     },
77:   }
78: }

80: const processedRules = new WeakSet<Rule>()

82: function processRule(
83:   rule: Rule,
84:   rewriter: ScopedSelectorRewriter,
85:   units: SelectorRewriteUnits,
86: ) {
87:   if (
88:     processedRules.has(rule) ||
89:     (rule.parent &&
90:       rule.parent.type === 'atrule' &&
91:       /-?keyframes$/.test((rule.parent as AtRule).name))
92:   ) {
93:     return
94:   }
95:   processedRules.add(rule)
96:   let deep = false
97:   let parent: Document | Container | undefined = rule.parent
98:   while (parent && parent.type !== 'root') {
99:     if ((parent as any)[units.wrap.deepKey]) {
100:       deep = true
101:       break
102:     }
103:     parent = parent.parent
104:   }
105:   rule.selector = selectorParser(selectorRoot => {
106:     selectorRoot.each(selector => {
107:       rewriter.rewriteSelector(
108:         rule,
109:         selector,
110:         selectorRoot,
111:         deep,
112:         false,
113:         units.slots,
114:         units.wrap,
115:         units.nodeTypes,
116:         units.deepSyntax,
117:         units.tokens,
118:         units.deepPseudos,
119:       )
120:     })
121:   }).processSync(rule.selector)
122: }

124: class ScopedSelectorRewriter {
125:   constructor(public id: string) {}
126: 
127:   rewriteSelector(
128:     rule: Rule,
129:     selector: selectorParser.Selector,
130:     selectorRoot: selectorParser.Root,
131:     deep: boolean,
132:     slotted: boolean,
133:     slots: SlotPseudoNames,
134:     wrap: NestedRuleWrap,
135:     nodeTypes: NestedNodeTypes,
136:     deepSyntax: DeprecatedDeepSyntax,
137:     tokens: CombinatorTokens,
138:     deepPseudos: DeepPseudoNames,
139:   ) {
140:     let node: selectorParser.Node | null = null
141:     let shouldInject = !deep
142:     // find the last child node to insert attribute selector
143:     selector.each(n => {
144:       // DEPRECATED ">>>" and "/deep/" combinator
145:       if (
146:         n.type === 'combinator' &&
147:         (n.value === deepSyntax.deprecatedDeep ||
148:           n.value === deepSyntax.deprecatedSlashDeep)
149:       ) {
150:         n.value = tokens.spaceCombinator
151:         n.spaces.before = n.spaces.after = ''
152:         warn(
153:           `the >>> and /deep/ combinators have been deprecated. ` +
154:             `Use :deep() instead.`,
155:         )
156:         return false
157:       }
158: 
159:       if (n.type === 'pseudo') {
160:         const { value } = n
161:         // deep: inject [id] attribute at the node before the ::v-deep
162:         // combinator.
163:         if (value === deepPseudos.deep || value === deepPseudos.vDeep) {
164:           ;(rule as any)[wrap.deepKey] = true
165:           if (n.nodes.length) {
166:             // .foo ::v-deep(.bar) -> .foo[xxxxxxx] .bar
167:             // replace the current node with ::v-deep's inner selector
168:             let last: selectorParser.Selector['nodes'][0] = n
169:             n.nodes[0].each(ss => {
170:               selector.insertAfter(last, ss)
171:               last = ss
172:             })
173:             // insert a space combinator before if it doesn't already have one
174:             const prev = selector.at(selector.index(n) - 1)
175:             if (!prev || !isSpaceCombinator(prev)) {
176:               selector.insertAfter(
177:                 n,
178:                 selectorParser.combinator({
179:                   value: tokens.spaceCombinator,
180:                 }),
181:               )
182:             }
183:             selector.removeChild(n)
184:           } else {
185:             // DEPRECATED usage
186:             // .foo ::v-deep .bar -> .foo[xxxxxxx] .bar
187:             warn(

199:         }

201:         // slot: use selector inside `::v-slotted` and inject [id + '-s']

205:           this.rewriteSelector(
206:             rule,
207:             n.nodes[0],
208:             selectorRoot,
209:             deep,
210:             true /* slotted */,
211:             slots,
212:             wrap,
213:             nodeTypes,
214:             deepSyntax,
215:             tokens,
216:             deepPseudos,
217:           )
218:           let last: selectorParser.Selector['nodes'][0] = n
219:           n.nodes[0].each(ss => {
220:             selector.insertAfter(last, ss)
221:             last = ss
222:           })
223:           // selector.insertAfter(n, n.nodes[0])
224:           selector.removeChild(n)
225:           // since slotted attribute already scopes the selector there's no
226:           // need for the non-slot attribute.
227:           shouldInject = false
228:           return false
229:         }
230: 
231:         // global: replace with inner selector and do not inject [id].
232:         // ::v-global(.foo) -> .foo
233:         if (value === ':global' || value === '::v-global') {
234:           selectorRoot.insertAfter(selector, n.nodes[0])
235:           selectorRoot.removeChild(selector)
236:           return false
237:         }
238:       }
239: 
240:       if (n.type === 'universal') {
241:         const prev = selector.at(selector.index(n) - 1)
242:         const next = selector.at(selector.index(n) + 1)
243:         // * ... {}
244:         if (!prev) {
245:           // * .foo {} -> .foo[xxxxxxx] {}
246:           if (next) {
247:             if (next.type === 'combinator' && next.value === ' ') {
248:               selector.removeChild(next)
249:             }
250:             selector.removeChild(n)
251:             return
252:           } else {
253:             // * {} -> [xxxxxxx] {}
254:             node = selectorParser.combinator({
255:               value: tokens.emptyCombinator,
256:             })
257:             selector.insertBefore(n, node)
258:             selector.removeChild(n)
259:             return false
260:           }
261:         }
262:         // .foo * -> .foo[xxxxxxx] *
263:         if (node) return
264:       }
265: 
266:       if (
267:         (n.type !== 'pseudo' && n.type !== 'combinator') ||
268:         (n.type === 'pseudo' &&
269:           (n.value === ':is' || n.value === ':where') &&
270:           !node)
271:       ) {
272:         node = n
273:       }
274:     })
275: 
276:     if (rule.nodes.some(node => node.type === nodeTypes.nestedType)) {
277:       const deep = (rule as any)[wrap.deepKey]
278:       const decls = rule.nodes.filter(node => node.type === nodeTypes.declType)
279:       if (!deep && decls.length) {
280:         for (const decl of decls) {
281:           rule.removeChild(decl)
282:         }
283:         const hostRule = new Rule({
284:           nodes: decls,
285:           selector: wrap.hostSelector,

295:         ;(node as selectorParser.Pseudo).nodes.forEach(value =>

301:             slotted,
302:             slots,

304:             nodeTypes,
305:             deepSyntax,
306:             tokens,
307:             deepPseudos,
308:           ),
309:         )
310:         shouldInject = false
311:       }
312:     }
313:

316:     } else {

318:       // the attribute selectors are prepended rather than appended.

320:       selector.first.spaces.before = ''

/**
 * Copied from https://github.com/MananTank/validate-html-nesting
 * with ISC license
 *
 * To avoid runtime dependency on validate-html-nesting
 * This file should not change very often in the original repo
 * but we may need to keep it up-to-date from time to time.
 */

import {
  createNestedSelectorParts,
  type NestedNodeTypes,
} from './transforms/transformStyle'
import type {
  CombinatorTokens,
  DeepPseudoNames,
  DeprecatedDeepSyntax,
} from './parserOptions'

/**
 * returns true if given parent-child nesting is valid HTML
 */
export function isValidHTMLNesting(parent: string, child: string): boolean {
  // if we know the list of children that are the only valid children for the given parent
  if (parent in onlyValidChildren) {
    return onlyValidChildren[parent].has(child)
  }

  // if we know the list of parents that are the only valid parents for the given child
  if (child in onlyValidParents) {
    return onlyValidParents[child].has(parent)
  }

  // if we know the list of children that are NOT valid for the given parent
  if (parent in knownInvalidChildren) {
    // check if the child is in the list of invalid children
    // if so, return false
    if (knownInvalidChildren[parent].has(child)) return false
  }

  // if we know the list of parents that are NOT valid for the given child
  if (child in knownInvalidParents) {
    // check if the parent is in the list of invalid parents
    // if so, return false
    if (knownInvalidParents[child].has(parent)) return false
  }

  return true
}

const headings = new Set(['h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'h6'])
const emptySet = new Set([])

/**
 * maps element to set of elements that can be it's children, no other */
const onlyValidChildren: Record<string, Set<string>> = {
  head: new Set([
    'base',
    'basefront',
    'bgsound',
    'link',
    'meta',
    'title',
    'noscript',
    'noframes',
    'style',
    'script',
    'template',
  ]),
  optgroup: new Set(['option']),
  select: new Set(['optgroup', 'option', 'hr']),
  // table
  table: new Set(['caption', 'colgroup', 'tbody', 'tfoot', 'thead']),
  tr: new Set(['td', 'th']),
  colgroup: new Set(['col']),
  tbody: new Set(['tr']),
  thead: new Set(['tr']),
  tfoot: new Set(['tr']),
  // these elements can not have any children elements
  script: emptySet,
  iframe: emptySet,
  option: emptySet,
  textarea: emptySet,
  style: emptySet,
  title: emptySet,
}

/** maps elements to set of elements which can be it's parent, no other */
const onlyValidParents: Record<string, Set<string>> = {
  // sections
  html: emptySet,
  body: new Set(['html']),
  head: new Set(['html']),
  // table
  td: new Set(['tr']),
  colgroup: new Set(['table']),
  caption: new Set(['table']),
  tbody: new Set(['table']),
  tfoot: new Set(['table']),
  col: new Set(['colgroup']),
  th: new Set(['tr']),
  thead: new Set(['table']),
  tr: new Set(['tbody', 'thead', 'tfoot']),
  // data list
  dd: new Set(['dl', 'div']),
  dt: new Set(['dl', 'div']),
  // other
  figcaption: new Set(['figure']),
  // li: new Set(["ul", "ol"]),
  summary: new Set(['details']),
  area: new Set(['map']),
} as const

/** maps element to set of elements that can not be it's children, others can */
const knownInvalidChildren: Record<string, Set<string>> = {
  p: new Set([
    'address',
    'article',
    'aside',
    'blockquote',
    'center',
    'details',
    'dialog',
    'dir',
    'div',

    'form',
    'h1',

    'section',

    'ul',
  ]),
  svg: new Set([
    'b',
    'blockquote',
    'br',
    'code',
    'dd',
    'div',
    'dl',
    'dt',
    'em',
    'embed',
    'h1',

    'hr',
    'i',

    's',
    'small',
    'span',
    'strong',
    'sub',
    'sup',
    'table',
    'u',
    'ul',
    'var',
  ]),
} as const

/** maps element to set of elements that can not be it's parent, others can */
const knownInvalidParents: Record<string, Set<string>> = {
  a: new Set(['a']),
  button: new Set(['button']),
  dd: new Set(['dd', 'dt']),
  dt: new Set(['dd', 'dt']),
  form: new Set(['form']),
  li: new Set(['li']),
  h1: headings,
  h2: headings,
  h3: headings,
  h4: headings,
  h5: headings,
  h6: headings,
}

export class NestedRuleWrap {
  constructor(
    public hostSelector: string,
    public deepKey: string,
  ) {}
}

export interface NestedRuleContext {
  wrap: NestedRuleWrap
  nodeTypes: NestedNodeTypes
  deepSyntax: DeprecatedDeepSyntax
  tokens: CombinatorTokens
  deepPseudos: DeepPseudoNames
}

export function createNestedRuleContext(): NestedRuleContext {
  const parts = createNestedSelectorParts()
  return {
    wrap: new NestedRuleWrap('&', '__deep'),
    nodeTypes: parts.nodeTypes,
    deepSyntax: parts.deepSyntax,
    tokens: parts.tokens,
    deepPseudos: parts.deepPseudos,
  }
}

part.text:
Fixed. Summary of changes:

**`packages/compiler-sfc/src/style/pluginScoped.ts`**
- In `rewriteSelector`, when a rule contains nested rules, declarations/comments are now also extracted from nested at-rule children (`@media`, `@container`, etc.) and wrapped into a `&` host rule via the new `extractAndWrapNodes` helper (pluginScoped.ts:276-287). The `&` rule is then visited by the `Rule` handler and gets `[data-v-...]` appended, producing `&[data-v-xxx] { ... }` inside the at-rule — matching the expected output in the issue.
- The helper also moves comments along with declarations (previously only decls), so comments inside a nested rule stay attached to the scoped declarations.

**`packages/compiler-dom/src/transforms/transformStyle.ts`**
- Added `commentType` to `NestedNodeTypes` so the postcss plugin can reference comment nodes through the shared units object.

Validation:
- `compileStyle.spec.ts` (including the previously failing "nesting selector with atrule and comment" case) and the full `compiler-sfc` suite pass (413 tests).
- `compiler-dom` + `compiler-core` suites pass (744 tests).
- Manual repro with `@media` and `@container` nested inside `.foo` now emits `&[data-v-7ba5bd90]` inside the at-rules, exactly as the issue expects; top-level `@media` rules remain untouched.
- `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, and Prettier all clean.
